game.text: Cleveland at Jacksonville, Sunday, October 19, 2014, 1 p.m. ET, EverBank Field
game.label: Game

attack.text: Make Cleveland defend one formation as several different plays. Shift Kelce and Lewis, run Outside Zone, show the same track into Boot Flood, come back with Counter, and release a back or tight end into the space the pressure leaves. Test how Dansby and Robertson exchange the crossers and how Whitner and Gipson fit the run; don't assume their answers from a stat sheet. Cleveland has nine takeaways. The ball goes to the open answer, not the most elaborate drawing.
attack.label: The matchup I am attacking

protect.text: Five more sacks, free hits on Cousins, early interceptions to Skrine or Haden, or a missed protection count with a new left guard. Tennessee was a win, but five sacks and the ball on the ground twice are problems to investigate. Defensively, no lost edge on Tate, uncovered Cameron seam or uncontested deep release by Lee. Special teams cannot donate short fields.
protect.label: What I must not give them

change_course.text: If Mingo or Kruger beats our edge help, condense the pass menu to SOLID, SCAT, movement throws and screened rush counters. If Cleveland rotates a safety into every run fit, attack behind that rotation; if the safeties stay deep, keep taking favorable run numbers. If Hoyer consistently beats our pressure picture with an immediate throw, replace the bluff with sound four-man rush and match coverage. If a medical decision changes the guard or nickel, reissue the affected assignments.
change_course.label: What would make me change course

contingency.text: Andrew Norwell takes the first-unit left-guard work beside Monroe and Linsley; Brewster is the interior relief. Alan Ball takes the nickel and Malcolm Butler the outside reserve job, with Prosinski the sixth defensive back and Phillips the safety reserve. These are the Week 7 answers if the October 15 reassessments do not clear Bitonio or Bouye. If either is cleared unexpectedly, I recheck the order, nickel and seven inactives with the medical staff before the final sheet.
contingency.label: If Bitonio or Bouye cannot dress

coverage_units.text: Westhoff moves Bouye's kicking assignments to the medically eligible Ball, Butler, Phillips and Prosinski group, with Todd Davis or the next dressed linebacker taking coverage work as needed. Keep Talib and Verner outside, Rambo and Trawick deep, and no emergency safety in an untaught exchange. Protect the new left guard with a real tackle-tight-end-back pickup plan. Aaron Donald is already in the first defensive-line group: he starts inside with Marks and has the interior pressure job in Nickel and Dime, while Roy Miller supplies the heavier interior run rotation.
coverage_units.label: Special coverage and substitution consequences

base_personnel.text: Use 12 and 11 as interchangeable pictures. The current order begins with Anderson at back and Kelce at tight end; Jones-Drew remains the proven Power, Counter, goal-line and four-minute answer, with no forced touch split. Kelce can attach or move; Lewis supplies the dependable attached surface, protection and receiving complement. Adams is X, Thielen H, Hawkins Z, with Hurns and Gabriel for rehearsed relief. Linsley makes the center declaration with Norwell at left guard while Bitonio is out. We keep two tight ends in the picture but do not release both against an uncovered rush threat.
base_personnel.label: Base personnel and roles

learn.text: How Cleveland's linebackers bump or travel with a 12-to-Empty shift; whether Whitner inserts on Power and the Outside Zone track; whether Gipson stays over the post; how Mingo and Kruger rush with a chip or moving launch point; and whether the defense switches the two shallow crossers in Bunch. We test the coverage, not label it ahead of the snap.
learn.label: The first things I want to learn

opening_approach.text: Show Outside Zone and its Boot from the same Wing alignment. Follow Power with Counter and protected Power Pass only after a safety declares. Use SHIFT Empty and Bunch to change the count with familiar receivers; mix quick throws and the back screen into the same series. The first fifteen ideas investigate alignments, then return to the call that created a favorable defender response. Short yardage, backed-up and scoring downs take their own calls.
opening_approach.label: Opening approach

third_down.text: Short: Power, Counter or the counted Inside Zone/Bubble. Medium: SCAT Stick, Mesh or Y-Cross; work the marker. Long: SOLID Y-Cross, Drive, protected Dagger, or Slow Screen against confirmed rush. Cousins states the blitz answer before the snap; five sacks in Tennessee make protection identification a practice priority, not proof of any one player's fault.
third_down.label: Third down

backed_up.text: Outside Zone, Inside Zone, Power and Stick SCAT. Two safe completions are better than one unprotected seven-step drop. No delayed gadget or blind reverse field.
backed_up.label: Backed up

red_zone.text: High: protected Cross, Power Pass and gated Boot. Low: Bunch Mesh, Snag, Power and Counter, with run-pass leverage clear to Cousins. Goal line: downhill gap run first; a pass needs a covered protection and clean release. No self-inflicted grounding or delay as in the Tennessee game.
red_zone.label: High red zone, low red zone, goal line

two_minute.text: Stick, Spacing, Drive, Mesh and Y-Cross from a personnel group that can stay on the field. The clock assistant gets the next snap, sideline options and timeout count to me early. The quarterback retains his practiced audible authority inside this reduced menu.
two_minute.label: Two-minute / hurry-up

four_minute.text: Run at the favorable fit with Anderson or Jones-Drew, then punish the loaded box with SOLID Y-Cross or a safe Boot. Play for first downs, not three automatic runs. Everyone knows the clock cost of a sack or incompletion before the series.
four_minute.label: Four-minute / protect a lead

sudden_change.text: Secure the first snap unless the defense already gave us the exact Power Pass or Boot trigger. Do not force a deep shot because we have a short field. Against an aggressive rush, the Slow Screen is our changeup.
sudden_change.label: Sudden change / shot opportunities

front.text: Aaron Donald is a first-unit interior lineman alongside Sen'Derrick Marks, with Mincey and the opposite edge completing the starting four. Donald attacks a guard or the center's protection relationship from a coached 3-technique, while Roy Miller rotates into heavier run surfaces. Under is the base against Tate and attached tight ends; Bear is the short-yardage answer, Nickel Even the spread response. Donald and Marks must keep their own run gaps before any twist. Daryl Smith declares the front, with Posluszny and Telvin Smith connected to the puller and cutback.
front.label: Base front and run fits

coverage.text: Give Hoyer a crowd at the line without giving him an easy pre-snap answer. Show the two A-gap threats, rotate safeties late, and most often send four with 1 Robber, Quarters or Cover 6 behind it. Use an actual fifth rusher with Fire 3 only when the hot route and contain are accounted for. Lee is the first receiver in our coverage count, Cameron's seam and crossing release the second. Talib and Verner stay on their outside sides; Ball handles the nickel until Bouye is medically cleared, and Butler is the outside reserve. Donald's interior push is the point of the pressure picture, not permission to vacate his gap.
coverage.label: Coverage and rush approach

discover.text: Does Mack reset the point when we mug both A-gaps, and where does Tate scan? Does Hoyer throw immediately against the threat picture or hold for a developing route? Does Lee change sides or go inside; does Cameron release across the formation? Keep Joe Thomas's edge and the quarterback's escape lane accounted for on every rush.
discover.label: What we need to discover early

matchups.text: Aaron Donald remains a first-unit interior starter and is featured in Nickel and Dime against Cleveland's interior protection, not held for a late series. Ball takes the nickel if Bouye remains out; Butler is the outside reserve; Prosinski is the sixth defensive back; Rambo and Trawick remain safeties. Talib and Verner keep outside assignments. No unsupported fixed shadow or automatic six-man rush.
matchups.label: Individual matchups / roles changed

kicking.text: Hawkins stays on kicks and punts, Hurns on the prepared punt-return alternative. Scobee, Anger and Kreiter remain the operation. Westhoff reviews the missed short field goal and the 25-yard punt at Tennessee without assigning blame before the film, rehearses placement and protection, and replaces Bouye's coverage work with eligible players. Cleveland's return volume merits clean vice, pursuit angles and no free penalty.
kicking.label: Return, coverage and operation instructions

endgame.text: Skalaski reports the actual down, distance, field, clock and timeout inventory before the fourth-down rule acts. No deciding from a hypothetical third-down outcome. Let the booth handle automatic reviews and the final two minutes. Use timeouts to preserve possession and a necessary call, not to compensate for a rushed substitution. Discuss clock risk with Cousins before two-minute and four-minute series.
endgame.label: Timeouts, challenges and endgame

participation.text: Reissue after exam. Norwell and Ball take the first work until the October 15 Bitonio and Bouye decisions; if either is cleared early, restore only a role he is medically allowed and has rehearsed. Reconcile the full seven inactives and kicking coverage before the game.
participation.label: If a medical assessment changes participation

tradeoff.text: The Flea Flicker is practice only, and new gadget installation and optional deep-shot repetitions give way to the line protection, nickel exchange and pressure disguise. Wednesday is the permitted padded practice, Thursday and Friday are helmets, Saturday the walkthrough; no work is recorded as completed by this plan.
tradeoff.label: What leaves the practice menu to make room

staff.text: I call both units. Tice keeps the offensive installation and situation relay; Bates brings Cousins's actual protection comfort; Crennel sends the defensive calls and reconciles Donald's rush with the coverage; Daryl Smith calls the front; Westhoff controls the kicking operation; Skalaski owns the clock and fourth-down feed. Let players challenge the picture in meetings, then make them show the answer without a prompt. Tell me which defender we are testing and what we will call when he changes. Keep the menu small enough to practice properly.
staff.label: Staff instructions

public.text: We won in Tennessee because we made plays and finished the fourth quarter. We also took five sacks. Cleveland is 4-1, has taken the ball away nine times and can run it. We have work to do, and the coaching staff starts with the protection plan and the defensive assignments.
public.label: Public position, if I am adding one

open_decisions.text: Bitonio's and Bouye's October 15 medical decisions, with the corresponding left-guard, nickel and seven-inactive confirmation. No personnel transaction is assumed. The final special-teams list follows the eligible 46.
open_decisions.label: Other open decisions

ready.text: The October 15 assessments, the Norwell/Linsley protection and Ball/Butler coverage checks, Donald's stunt and run-fit rehearsal, the kicking operation and the final legal 46 are confirmed before Sunday kickoff.
ready.label: Ready to lock after

responses.counter: Stay Nickel if the offense prevents substitution; own the back screen and scramble.

Bouye, Jordan Poyer, Charles Leno Jr., Kasim Edebali, Todd Davis, Hakeem Nicks; RB order: C.J. Anderson, Maurice Jones-Drew, Jonathan Grimes; WR order: Davante Adams, Adam Thielen, Andrew Hawkins, Allen Hurns, Taylor Gabriel, Hakeem Nicks; TE order: Travis Kelce, Marcedes Lewis, Marcel Jensen, Gator Hoskins; OL order: Eugene Monroe, Andrew Norwell, Corey Linsley, Trai Turner, Lane Johnson, Cornelius Lucas, Mike Brewster, Charles Leno Jr., Joel Bitonio; DL order: Jeremy Mincey, Aaron Donald, Sen'Derrick Marks, Andre Branch, Roy Miller, C.J. Mosley, Daniel Te'o-Nesheim, Kasim Edebali; LB order: Daryl Smith, Paul Posluszny, Telvin Smith, Sio Moore, Julian Stanford, Christian Jones, Todd Davis; Nickel: Alan Ball; Outside reserve corner: Malcolm Butler.
